You’re right to call that out — the wording was easy to misread.

**What I should have said clearly:**

- **`.\build.ps1` is run from the repo root**  
  `I:\NMSFM REPOS\Fire Fund App - CVE Fixes\NMSFM_FPF`  
  That only means “where the script lives / where you open PowerShell.” It does **not** mean “point IIS here.”

- **IIS must point at the web app’s content root** — the folder that is the actual ASP.NET site:  
  `I:\NMSFM REPOS\Fire Fund App - CVE Fixes\NMSFM_FPF\NMSFM`

So: **same machine / same repo / same build output**, but **not** the same directory as the folder where you ran the script. The script builds into `NMSFM\bin\` (and related outputs under `NMSFM`); IIS needs the **`NMSFM`** folder so it loads `Web.config`, `Global.asax`, and `bin\NMSFM.dll`.

**Short rule:**  
Run `build.ps1` from `NMSFM_FPF`; point the site at `NMSFM_FPF\NMSFM`.

Sorry for the confusion — pointing at the repo root is what caused **403.14**.
